reasoning_traces.think:
The genetic algorithm (GA) framework attempts to optimize DraftKings lineups by evolving populations over generations, mimicking natural selection. However, for problems with linear constraints such as salary caps and player limits, GA fails to guarantee global optima due to stochastic exploration and local minima entrapment. In contrast, Mixed Integer Linear Programming (MILP) offers deterministic, optimal solutions within polynomial time bounds for such structured problems. The GA's reliance on mutation and crossover introduces redundancy and inefficiency, especially when the search space is well-defined and convex. Furthermore, while GA may offer heuristic diversity in multi-lineup scenarios, MILP with iterative exclusions achieves superior diversity control without sacrificing optimality. Thus, the GA approach is mathematically inferior for this domain, rendering its adoption redundant and computationally wasteful.
